data.title: EXAT advances 2-phase Phuket expressway project
data.description: The Expressway Authority of Thailand (EXAT) is pressing ahead with a 34.6-kilometre expressway network in Phuket to ease traffic congestion and support the province's urban and tourism growth.

data.title: Chadchart defends switch to electric rubbish trucks
data.description: City Hall has defended a plan to replace rented diesel rubbish trucks with electric vehicles, saying the switch could cut energy costs by about 4.75 billion baht, or 54%, over five years.

data.title: B95bn irrigation project gets nod
data.description: A six-year irrigation project worth 95 billion baht has been approved to improve flood management in the lower eastern Chao Phraya basin and protect communities and economic areas across eight provinces, including Bangkok, said the government.

data.title: New rules clarify emergency care rights
data.description: The cabinet has endorsed revised rules for the Universal Coverage for Emergency Patients (UCEP) scheme, reaffirming that critically ill emergency patients must receive treatment without being charged until they are out of danger, for up to 72 hours.

data.title: CIB uncovers ex-abbot's millions
data.description: The Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) has uncovered more than 300 million baht in bank accounts linked to former Wat Phutthaisawan abbot Atichot Tanprasert and his close female associate as it widens its probe into suspected financial misconduct.

data.title: Anutin files defamation lawsuit against iLaw chief
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has filed a defamation lawsuit against iLaw director Yingcheep Atchanont over remarks linking him to alleged collusion in the 2024 Senate election, insisting the legal action is not intended to silence his critics.

data.title: South Africa intensifies hunt after eight women found dead
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - South African police are racing to crack the killings of at least eight women whose bodies have been found east of Johannesburg in two months, the latest on Tuesday.

data.title: Maduro ally pleads guilty to US money laundering charges
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Alex Saab, a former Venezuelan minister and close ally of ousted president Nicolas Maduro, pleaded guilty on Tuesday to money laundering under a deal with US prosecutors, court filings showed.

data.title: Finnish president Stubb speaks to AFP about Trump, Russia and saunas
data.description: HELSINKI - Finnish President Alexander Stubb said Donald Trump "pretty much does what he wants" and recommended staying calm in a world on edge, preferably with a sauna, in a freewheeling interview to AFP on Tuesday.

data.title: Empty benches as schools reopen in Venezuela's quake-hit Guaira
data.description: LA GUAIRA (VENEZUELA) - Schools in Venezuela's quake-scarred coastal state of La Guaira were deserted on Tuesday, a day after the start of the new school year, with many parents opting to keep children home for fear of further deadly tremors.

data.title: Trump says Kennedy Center to close after judge bars name change
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that the Kennedy Center will close down -- possibly for good -- after a judge ruled his name cannot be added onto the famed arts institution's exterior.

data.title: Trump decries ‘horrible’ Supreme Court mail-in ballot ruling
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump assailed the Supreme Court on Tuesday after it denied his request to lift an order halting his divisive plan to restrict mail-in voting — accusing the court of allowing itself to be cowed by Democrats.

data.title: Brazil’s top court probes judge’s ties to jailed banker
data.description: BRASILIA - Brazil’s Supreme Court on Tuesday began examining one of its top justice’s ties to a jailed banker, in an unprecedented crisis that has eclipsed the country’s presidential election campaign.

data.title: Accused senators vow to fight charges
data.description: Senators accused of irregularities in the 2024 Senate election have vowed to fight the charges after the Election Commission (EC) decided to refer cases against 77 people, including 26 serving senators, to the Supreme Court.

data.title: Udon Thani counting down to international horticultural expo
data.description: Udon Thani is preparing to welcome visitors from Thailand and around the world to an international horticultural exposition starting on Nov 1 and running until March 14 next year.

data.title: Denmark says Russian frigate fired flares at helicopter
data.description: COPENHAGEN - Denmark and Russia were at a war of words Tuesday after Danish authorities accused a Russian frigate of firing flares at a Danish military helicopter.

data.title: China warns against space ‘battlefield’
data.description: PARIS - China on Tuesday warned against turning outer space into a “battlefield” and Russia said it must be “free from any weapon” after the United States confirmed for the first time that it has arms deployed in orbit above the Earth.

data.title: Si Rat-Outer Ring Road tolls to rise from Dec 15
data.description: Tolls on the Prachim Ratthaya Expressway, also known as the Si Rat-Outer Ring Road Expressway, will increase by 15-35 baht from Dec 15, with the rate for four-wheel vehicles rising from 65 baht to 80 baht in accordance with the terms of the concession agreement.

data.title: Nairobi to host 2029 world athletics championships
data.description: PARIS - Nairobi will host the 2029 world outdoor athletics championships, beating off competition from London, Munich and Rome to become the first African hosts, World Athletics announced on Tuesday.

data.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
data.description: VILNIUS, Lithuania - NATO fighter jets shot down a drone over Lithuania, the Baltic state’s president said Tuesday, in the latest security incident on the alliance’s eastern flank during Russia’s war with Ukraine.

data.title: Smuggled coffee seizures a first in southern Thailand
data.description: Customs officials in southern Thailand have seized more than 20 tonnes of illegally imported green coffee beans this year, as part of a wider crackdown that has resulted in seizures of goods worth 216 million baht.

data.title: Ukraine winemakers defy war to make a splash at home
data.description: BEREHOVE — As this year's harvest season entered full swing, a winery in western Ukraine had an additional task to oversee: installing solar panels to help it weather blackouts caused by Russian military strikes.

data.title: Building organisations that transform faster than technology changes
data.description: Only a few years ago, the breakthrough in generative artificial intelligence (AI) allowed us for the first time to ask a machine a question and receive a remarkably human-like answer. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 represent the latest frontiers in what machines can now do across coding, computer use and scientific work. But the real problem for business leaders is the speed at which the boundary of what machines can do keeps moving.

data.title: Greek neo-Nazi exits prison, vows return to politics
data.description: DOMOKOS — The former spokesman of Greek neo-Nazi party Golden Dawn, Ilias Kasidiaris, was released from prison Tuesday and vowed a return to politics, having already drawn attention from Elon Musk.

data.title: Saudi Arabia vows to respond 'firmly' to Houthi attacks
data.description: SANAA — Saudi Arabia vowed Tuesday to respond "firmly" to attacks by Yemen's Houthis, after the Iran-backed fighters wounded 13 people in the kingdom in an assault using ballistic missiles and drones.
